The Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt after he refused to answer questions, citing his Fifth Amendment rights following a presidential pardon.

The Bright Side:
This conflict forces a public debate on the limits of congressional subpoena power versus individual constitutional rights.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHO vs. WHAT error. They frame it as a procedural WHAT (contempt), but the reality is a personal WHO (Fauci) vendetta.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic power-hoarding loop. By framing a constitutional right as a crime, the committee creates a pretext to punish a political opponent, projecting their own partisan motives onto the witness.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The force of the pretext outweighs the stated goal of oversight.

The Unavoidable Truth: Constitutional rights apply to all witnesses, regardless of political status.

The Unavoidable Lie: This vote is purely about enforcing legislative procedure.

This is a structural collapse of legislative norms. By weaponizing contempt, the committee erodes the very legal framework they claim to uphold.
